clue.text: Biggles' friend about to go abroad after land which Nelson turns his back on

definitions.text: which Nelson turns his back on

indicators.note: after places the friend-and-verb piece behind the word for land

parts.note: a land or country is a nation

indicators.note: about means the friend's name wraps round the foreign verb

parts.note: Algy (Algernon Lacey) is the sidekick of the fictional flying ace Biggles
aller is French for to go, so 'to go' as said abroad

explanation.surface: An odd story of Biggles' sidekick heading overseas from a country Nelson ignores.
explanation.walkthrough: Biggles is the fictional British flying ace of W.E. Johns's books. Nelson's statue in Trafalgar Square faces south, its back to the gallery on the square's north side.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson's statue atop his column in Trafalgar Square looks south, its back to the London art museum on the square's north side.

clue.text: See 6
House getting cast aside on Monopoly square

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes first

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it out
GO is the starting square on a Monopoly board

explanation.surface: A house is lost on a particular square of the board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the bingo call for a full card; in the surface it looks like the Monopoly property.
explanation.definitionFit: In the numbers game, a winner shouts 'House!', and the game itself is also called house or housey-housey.

clue.text: See 18
Doctor having admitted crime, it's curtains for him!

indicators.note: having admitted means the doctor's abbreviation takes the crime inside it

parts.note: rape is a serious crime

explanation.surface: A medic who confessed to a crime faces the end of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's curtains for him' suggests doom, but literally a fabric seller deals in curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth merchant sells fabrics including curtain material, so curtains are his trade.

clue.text: Left with bit of fish, I left artist with it beneath river in the 1

indicators.note: in a down entry, what lies beneath the river follows it

parts.note: the Arno is the river through Florence
port is the left side of a ship
a fin is part of a fish
port is the left side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter cobbles together a fish part and the river, oddly abandoning things along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 1' points to 1 Down, the National Gallery in London, where Van Eyck's double portrait of a merchant and his wife hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Eyck's famous 1434 painting of the merchant and his wife hangs in London's main national art museum.

clue.text: Article with 16 read out so as to press charges

indicators.note: read out means the pieces are heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: the article A with 16 (the answer to 16 Across, i.e. letters), here the letters Qs

explanation.surface: An item with some text is read aloud in court before a charge is laid.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, A and the plural of the letter Q come out as 'uh-kyooz'.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone is to charge them formally with an offence, i.e. to press charges against them.

clue.text: Cryptic set in two minutes to which half the country may subscribe?

definitions.text: to which half the country may subscribe?

indicators.note: something cryptic is puzzling and disguised, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter finishes a crossword in two minutes, enjoyed by half the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the country' means the female half, who alone may join this British women's organisation, known for jam and Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: Membership of the British community group for women is open only to women, roughly half the population.

clue.text: A throwback by literary cameraman chopping wood — one wielding axe

parts.note: a throw is a lob, and back turns it round

indicators.note: chopping means the word wood is cut away from the writer's name

parts.note: Christopher Isherwood wrote 'I am a camera', so he is the literary cameraman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer of old Berlin, given a throw, sets about felling timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwback' is one word doing two things: LOB (throw) turned back to BOL. 'chopping' removes WOOD from ISHERWOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abolishes something takes the axe to it, cutting it out entirely.

clue.text: Half of document taken to one side

indicators.note: half of takes the first three of six letters of the synonym for document

parts.note: a record is a document

explanation.surface: Half of a paper is set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' trims RECORD to REC; the definition is 'one side', a page of a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf, is one side of it.

clue.text: Perhaps 9 or 10 writhing in clutches of feline (head ripped off)

indicators.note: in clutches of means the jumbled number is held inside the cat's word
head ripped off removes the first letter from the cat

parts.note: a tiger is a feline

indicators.note: writhing means the letters of the number twist into a new order

parts.note: 10 is ten

explanation.surface: Some number squirms in the claws of a beheaded big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps 9' is the definition: nine is one example of a whole number. 'writhing' scrambles the number and 'head ripped off' beheads the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a whole number, an example of the mathematical class of numbers without fractions.

clue.text: Stick in the shade for effect

indicators.note: in means the stick goes inside the colour

parts.note: puce is a purplish-brown shade
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A stick placed in the shade for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect' is the verb, to bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect a change is to bring it about, to create or yield it.

clue.text: Bread rolls to appear unaltered

indicators.note: rolling the word over leaves it looking the same: it reads identically both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Bread rolls look the same as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' looks like baked goods but means turned over end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian flatbread, baked in a tandoor, is a kind of bread.

clue.text: Soil breakers, one passing through common, cutting marks

indicators.note: cutting means one piece slices into the middle of the marks

parts.note: scars are marks

indicators.note: passing through means the one goes inside the word for common

parts.note: rife means common, widespread
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Ploughing tools run across a shared field, leaving scars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' is an adjective here (widespread), not a stretch of village grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarifiers are tools that loosen and break up the surface of soil or turf.

clue.text: See 17
Europeans claiming the 23 is learning

indicators.note: claiming means the Europeans take hold of the royal cipher inside them

parts.note: Letts are Latvians, a European people
23 Down is queen, and ER is the royal cipher for Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Europeans claim the monarch is educated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 23' sends you to 23 Down, QUEEN; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters means scholarship or learning, as in a man of letters.

clue.text: Slough about a month for chef's assistant

indicators.note: about means the marsh word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a slough is a bog, a fen
Nov is the abbreviation for November

explanation.surface: A town in Berkshire hosts a month of cookery help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the English town but is a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A convection oven circulating hot air helps a cook in the kitchen.

clue.text: Thing wriggling inside fruit stem with head bitten off taking long time before fury shown in the 1

indicators.note: before puts the long time ahead of the fury
inside means the jumbled word sits within the fruit

parts.note: a fig is a fruit

indicators.note: wriggling means the letters squirm into a new order
with head bitten off loses the first letter of stem

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a long time
ire is fury

explanation.surface: A creature wriggles in fruit, its stem nibbled, before an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wriggling' scrambles THING to GHTIN. 'the 1' is 1 Down, the National Gallery, where Turner's painting of the old warship hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Turner's 1839 painting of the old warship towed to be broken up is displayed in London's National Gallery.

clue.text: Shocking rift over works in the 1

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A shocking split arises over some artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like paintings, but signals the anagram; Leonardo's painting hangs in the National Gallery (1 Down).
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci's version of the Madonna in a grotto is a painting in London's National Gallery.

clue.text: Ready to sell goat that's wild

indicators.note: that's wild means the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Prepared to sell a goat that has gone feral.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all prepared for departure means being ready.

clue.text: Position taken by terrorist leader, which brings devastation

indicators.note: taken by means the position word comes first, then the leader

parts.note: a locus is a position or place

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of terrorist

explanation.surface: A position seized by the head of a terror group causes ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Swarms of the insect strip crops bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming grasshoppers devour crops, bringing devastation, as in the biblical plagues.

clue.text: Girl that endlessly collects wood

indicators.note: collects means the trimmed word gathers the wood inside it
endlessly means the last letter of that is dropped

parts.note: elm is a wood

explanation.surface: A girl endlessly gathers firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts THAT to THA, which 'collects' ELM: TH-ELM-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a girl's name, as in the film Thelma and Louise.

clue.text: Move to the left?

definitions.meaning: to move at a jogging pace
a Trotskyist, a far-left political activist, is informally called this

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the political sense: a Trot is someone on the hard left.
explanation.definitionFit: A jog is a gentle move, and a Trotskyist is a person on the political left.

clue.text: Top piece of baroque engineering

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fine feature of ornate old architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' and 'piece' suggest chess: the queen is the strongest piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The strongest piece in chess, the top piece, or the top card in a suit below the king.

clue.text: Feed baby no more, having swallowed document

indicators.note: having swallowed means the word for no more takes the document inside it

parts.note: late means deceased, no more
an act is a legal document

explanation.surface: A mother stops feeding her baby after taking in some paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feed baby no more' reads as weaning; the definition is just 'Feed baby'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lactate is to produce milk, which is how a mother feeds a baby.

clue.text: Holidaymaker Leon entertained by baby

indicators.note: entertained by means the author's name goes inside the baby

parts.note: a tot is a baby
Leon Uris was the American novelist of Exodus

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker called Leon is amused by a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leon' looks like a first name but stands for the novelist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a person travelling for pleasure, a holidaymaker.

clue.text: One was recently asleep through part of flight

definitions.meaning: someone who gets up from bed, having been asleep till just now
the vertical part of a step in a flight of stairs

explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a staircase, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: An early or late getter-up, and the upright board between treads on a staircase.

clue.text: Food for thought from militant feminists?

definitions.text: Food for thought from militant feminists?

parts.words: Food for thought from militant feminists?
parts.note: a vegetable whose name, split into three words, sounds like a demand to eject the male

explanation.walkthrough: Split as MAN GET OUT, this pea pod reads as a slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat edible pea pod is food; split into words it is an order for men to leave.
